[HUMAN DECISION NEEDED — type name conflict between bead text and crate scaffolding]

Two human-authored sources disagree on the public type name:

(a) Bead text — JMAP-v9py.12 and JMAP-v9py.13 both say 'Sha256Digest' (capital D).
(b) Workspace AGENTS.md crate map + the PLAN.md scaffolded under JMAP-v9py.11 — both say 'Sha256' (no Digest suffix).

JMAP-v9py.12 was implemented as 'jmap_cid_types::Sha256' (matching (b)), so it currently does NOT match the wording of this bead's acceptance criterion (which says 'Option<jmap_cid_types::Sha256Digest>'). The error type was named 'Sha256DigestError' regardless — that wasn't a conflict point.

Two paths forward:

PATH 1 — KEEP 'Sha256' (recommended): edit this bead's acceptance to read 'Option<jmap_cid_types::Sha256>'. Rationale: the crate name 'jmap-cid-types' already implies digest context; 'cid_types::Sha256' reads naturally; 'cid_types::Sha256Digest' is verbose. The workspace AGENTS.md crate map already cites 'Sha256'.

PATH 2 — RENAME to 'Sha256Digest': rename in jmap-cid-types (~5 min: rename struct, public re-export in lib.rs, 19 test names if the agent renames them too, doc comments). Then this bead's acceptance is unchanged.

I'm leaving JMAP-v9py.13 OPEN and labeled 'human' so the autonomous loop skips it and Mark picks the path. JMAP-v9py.14 (supports_cid on Session) does not depend on this naming decision and is being worked next.
